## sheet: Batch Zero FAQs
				
	Batch Zero Readiness FAQs 			
	Current as of July 21, 2026 (Version Eight)			
	Disclaimer:  This question-and-answer document is provided solely for informational purposes. In the event of any conflict with the ERCOT Protocols or Planning Guide, those authorities shall govern. ERCOT may update or revise answers as it receives additional questions and information. Nothing in this document constitutes an interpretation or guidance by ERCOT, or is otherwise binding, in proceedings at the Public Utility Commission of Texas, including Project No. 58481, Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards Under PURA § 37.0561.  Unless otherwise noted, capitalized terms are defined consistent with the ERCOT Protocols.			
	Macro-topic	ID	Question	Answer
	Batch Zero eligibility and qualifications	1	Do already energized loads automatically qualify for inclusion in Batch Zero? 	Under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(a) and (b), already energized loads are included as base load subject to the Interconnecting Large Load Entity (ILLE) and applicable Interconnecting Transmission Service Provider (TSP) or Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider (DSP) providing necessary modeling and technical information.  The ILLE and TSP or DSP should consult the Load Information Form to determine what additional information is required for modeling purposes.

		2	Does all long lead equipment mean the ILLE's substation equipment, all load facility equipment, or both?
	All long lead equipment as used in Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(iii) includes the ILLE's interconnection equipment, e.g., transformers and breakers.
		3	What is the definition of an end-use customer in Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(v)?	The end-use customer is the customer that will take electric service at the site of the Large Load development.  The ILLE must be able to demonstrate an existing legally binding connection linking itself, the Large Load development, and the ultimate retail customer.  Execution of a retail electric service agreement can serve as evidence that the ILLE is the end-use customer.  

		4	Is a purchase and sale agreement that includes a termination right, typically referred to as a due diligence period, valid for purposes of the site control criteria?
	The inclusion of a right to terminate in a purchase and sale agreement remains a valid purchase and sale agreement for purposes of PGRR145.
		5	Can ERCOT provide confirmation that a Large Load meets the eligibility criteria for its selected inclusion path before August 7, 2026?	ERCOT will evaluate submitted information and notify Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs of each Large Load’s classification and Batch Zero inclusion status by August 7, 2026. However, ERCOT strongly encourages Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs to provide the documentation identified in PGRR145, NPRR1325, and the ERCOT Large Load Integration page as early as possible.  ERCOT will endeavor to review submitted materials and provide prompt feedback on the submission. 

		6	What information does an ILLE need to disclose to satisfy the requirements in paragraphs (2) and (3) of Section 9.7?	To satisfy paragraph (2) of Section 9.7, an ILLE must disclose its plans, expected timing, and progress for site-related studies and engineering services required before energization.  Similarly, for paragraph (3) of Section 9.7, the ILLE must disclose its plans, expected timing, and current progress for obtaining non-ministerial discretionary approvals from state and local regulatory authorities required for the development before energization.  An ILLE is not required to provide its actual site-related studies or documents related to the ILLE’s efforts to obtain non-ministerial discretionary approvals.  However, ERCOT may request such information to verify the ILLE's attestation; an ILLE that cannot substantiate its attestation is subject to having the Large Load project removed from Batch Zero.
		7	Will the transfer of a Large Load interconnection request to another entity impact the inclusion of the Large Load in Batch Zero prior to the eligibility deadlines in PGRR145?	A transfer of the Large Load interconnection request to a new entity will not impact the inclusion and classification of the Large Load in Batch Zero.  However, the new ILLE must meet the applicable eligibility criteria. The Interconnecting TSP should send ERCOT an updated LIF to reflect the new ILLE. Any other changes, including but not limited to the load design, end use activity, point of interconnection, or other changes that might impact the electrical characteristics may impact Batch Zero qualification. These other changes will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
		8	Can an interconnection request projected to qualify as base load be split so that the initial portion of the LCP qualifies as base load while the remainder of the LCP enters Batch Zero as studied load instead? Both portions would rely on the same set of studies for qualification.	ERCOT has determined splitting an interconnection request in this way is permitted under PGRR145.
		9	Will an ILLE be deemed ineligible or disqualified from Batch Zero if the phased energization schedule disclosed in response to paragraph (4) of Section 9.7 does not match the LCP in the Batch Zero Load Information Form?	No.  The ILLE is required to disclose its phased energization schedule and the schedule should match the LCP in the Batch Zero Load Information Form.  However, if there is a mismatch, the ILLE will not be deemed ineligible or disqualified.  ERCOT will use the LCP in the Batch Zero Load Information Form to model the Large Load in the Batch Zero Interconnection Study.
		10	If a Large Load is entering Batch Zero as base load through Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e), and has an energization date in 2028 or later, may the ILLE order all equipment with a lead time of at least 18 months at a future date?	No.  To satisfy Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(iii), the ILLE must be able to attest that it has ordered prior to July 10, 2026 all equipment with a lead time of at least 18 months.
		11	If a Large Load is entering Batch Zero as base load through Section 9.2.1.1(1)(f), and is energizing in 2028 or later, does it have to have obtained all discretionary approvals?	Yes, to satisfy Section 9.2.1.1(1)(f)(iii), the ILLE must have obtained all discretionary approvals.
		12	May an ILLE rely on an affiliate to satisfy the eligibility criteria in Sections 9.2.1.1(1) and 9.2.1.2(1)?	Yes, an ILLE may rely on an affiliate to meet the eligibility criteria.  The ILLE's affiliate must qualify as an affiliate under a definition adapted from subparagraphs (A) through (E) of 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.5(3).  An ILLE relying on an affiliate must note that reliance in the first reserved field in Section 4 of the Batch Zero LIF and complete and submit the Affiliate Form posted on the Large Load Integration page.  The ILLE must complete the Affiliate Form for each affiliate it relies on to meet the eligibility criteria.
		13	Under what condition may an ILLE rely on the actions of a non-affiliated third party to satisfy one or more eligibility criteria?	An ILLE may satisfy one or more eligibility criteria through the actions of a non-affiliated entity that has been designated by the ILLE to perform such actions as the ILLE’s agent under a contractual arrangement.  The ILLE must note that it designated a non-affiliated entity to satisfy one or more eligibility criteria in the second reserved field in Section 4 of the Batch Zero LIF.  There is not an additional form.  However, during the verification process, ERCOT may request a copy of the contractual arrangement and evidence that the non-affiliated entity satisfied the eligibility criteria on behalf of the ILLE.
		14	Can ILLE/TSP request more than one eligibility path for Batch Zero?	No. An ILLE may only request inclusion under a single Batch Zero eligibility pathway. The Interconnecting TSP/DSP should identify the applicable eligibility path in the submission package and provide the documentation and attestations required for that path.
		15	What does Initial Energization mean?	Initial Energization is defined in the ERCOT Protocols as, “[t]he first time a Generation Resource, Energy Storage Resources (ESR), Settlement Only Generator (SOG), or Large Load facility’s equipment connects to the ERCOT System during commissioning of the new or modified Generation Resource, SOG, or Large Load.”
		16	Where the eligibility criteria in Section 9.2.1.1(1) require a binding contract or could be satisfied by the existence of a binding contract, is it acceptable for the contract to include placeholders for future work?	No.  A contract that includes agreement to address material terms in a future agreement, account for significant contingencies, or finalize placeholders functions more like a provisional agreement than a binding contract required by Section 9.2.1.1(1).  As the PUCT Staff’s April 13, 2026, memo in Project No. 59142 explains, the eligibility criteria are designed to identify Large Load developments that have reached a state of “advanced project maturity” and “intermediate project maturity.”  A contract that leaves material terms to a future agreement, significant contingencies, or placeholders is not evidence of intermediate maturity and falls further short of the advanced threshold.
		17	The Affiliate Form requires a signature from a person with binding over the ILLE and a person with binding authority over the Affiliate.  Is it acceptable for a person within a parent company to sign on behalf of both?	Yes. The Affiliate Form permits a single individual to sign in both capacities, provided that person is a representative, official, officer, or other authorized person with binding authority over the ILLE and the Affiliate independently.
		18	How will ERCOT evaluate information included in Section 1E of the Batch Zero Load Information Form (LIF) for Large Loads that are not pursuing WLPUN?	Regardless of whether the interconnecting Large Load intends to operate as a WLPUN or simply co-locate with a generator, the information requested in Section 1E of the Batch Zero LIF helps ERCOT process the interconnection requests.  In Section 2, if the ILLE intends to interconnect as a WLPUN, the Interconnecting DSP or TSP should select the “WLPUN” option in the Eligibility Path pull-down menu and the “Studied Load/PCLR/WLPUN” option in the Entry Path pull-down menu.  If the ILLE intends simply to co-locate with a generator, the Interconnecting DSP or TSP should select the “Studied Load” option in the Eligibility Path pull-down menu and the “Studied Load/PCLR/WLPUN” option in the Entry Path pull-down menu.  The proper selection of Eligibility and Entry paths ensures that Section 3 lists and displays the correct information required for submission.
		19	If a Large Load submitted as base load is ultimately classified as studied load can the ILLE submit Form W or Form X to elect PCLR or WLPUN status?	Yes, but it must make such a designation by July 10th.  If an ILLE seeking base load eligibility and entry into Batch Zero desires a backup strategy if its Large Load is ultimately classified as a studied load, the ILLE may conditionally request to be studied as a PCLR or WLPUN by submitting Form W or Form X by July 10th along with its base-load submission.  If the Large Load qualifies as base load, ERCOT will disregard the form.
	Study process and timelines	20	What are the key deadlines for inclusion in Batch Zero? 	The primary Batch Zero milestones are: 
*May 28, 2026 – Last date a study submitted to ERCOT is guaranteed review by July 10
*July 10, 2026 – Deadline for ILLEs seeking treatment as base load to have satisfied the applicable Batch Zero eligibility requirements, including submission of any required materials, including dynamic models and dynamic data packages where applicable
*July 24, 2026 – Deadline for Interconnecting DSPs/TSPs to submit to ERCOT all required Batch Zero materials and for TSPs to submit stability-study impact determinations, if applicable
*August 7, 2026 – ERCOT deadline by which it will notify TSPs/DSPs of Batch Zero inclusion and classification outcomes and dynamic model deficiencies
*August 31, 2026 – Final deadline to resolve outstanding dynamic model/data deficiencies; Large Loads with unresolved issues are excluded from Batch Zero

		21	How should a Large Load proceed if its eligibility pathway changes near the July 10 deadline?	It depends. Section 9.3.1(2) permits an ILLE to reconcile its financial security if its classification changes from base load to studied load. Where additional financial security is required due to reclassification, the ILLE generally has seven Business Days to satisfy the applicable requirement. Failure to satisfy the required financial security obligations may result in exclusion from Batch Zero. There is not a reconciliation period that works in reverse. Therefore, an ILLE that is unsure whether it will qualify as base load or studied load should submit as if it will be base load, and take advantage of the reconciliation period should ERCOT classify it as studied load.
		22	Should outdated or no-longer-achievable Load Commissioning Plans (LCPs) be updated before submission?	The LCP should reflect the Large Load's current information at the time of submission. If the Large Load's schedule for connecting the Large Load in increments has changed, the LCP should be updated accordingly. ERCOT has indicated that it expects a practical and achievable LCP rather than a schedule that is known to be outdated or no longer attainable. 

		23	If a Large Load has not yet started the scoping process, can it still realistically qualify for Batch Zero? 	Large Loads that have not yet completed a kickoff meeting by May 21, 2026 face a highly compressed timeline to complete scoping, studies, ERCOT review, and any required restudies before the July 10, 2026 sunset. The current Planning Guide allows the TSP, ERCOT, and any directly affected TSPs up to 35 Business Days to approve a study scope after a kickoff meeting is held. ERCOT will make every effort to review study scopes through the July 10, 2026 sunset. Even so, Large Loads that have not had a kickoff meeting before May 21, 2026, may not get an approved scope prior to July 10, 2026. 

		24	Will ERCOT continue conducting study reviews through July 10, 2026? 
	ERCOT is committed to continuing study reviews through the July 10, 2026 sunset date.  However, ERCOT cannot guarantee that studies submitted after May 28, 2026 will be reviewed before July 10, 2026.
		25	Are Large Loads guaranteed approval if the Transmission Service Provider submits studies before the July 10 cutoff? 	No. Studies submitted before July 10, 2026 are not guaranteed approval. ERCOT will continue reviewing studies under the current LLIS process through July 10, but submitted studies must still satisfy the applicable Planning Guide requirements. If ERCOT identifies deficiencies, incomplete information, or material changes to study assumptions, then clarification or restudy may be required. Additionally, ERCOT cannot guarantee that new or updated study reports submitted after May 28, 2026 will be reviewed by July 10, 2026.

		26	For base load, what information can be corrected after July 10 versus considered missing or incomplete?	ERCOT may allow cure of identified dynamic model deficiencies through August 31, 2026. In addition, ERCOT and the Interconnecting TSP/DSP may permit administrative corrections, clarification requests, or minor submission errors identified during the review process (e.g., typographical errors or incorrect references). However, the post–July 10 review period is not intended to allow submission of materially missing eligibility items or completion of requirements that were not satisfied by the applicable July 10 deadline (e.g., financial security, required commitments, or required attestations). Failure to resolve identified dynamic model deficiencies by August 31, 2026 results in removal from Batch Zero.

		27	How does ERCOT handle studies that become invalid because of other Large Loads meeting milestones ahead of the studied Large Load? 

	PGRR145 establishes a formal validation framework in Section 9.2.1.4. ERCOT will evaluate whether prior studies remain valid by assessing whether Large Loads with earlier approval dates were included within the applicable study area assumptions. Large Loads whose studies no longer reflect the evolving system conditions may be reclassified into the “load to be studied and allocated” category.
		28	In the Batch Zero Interconnection Study, will ERCOT allocate the total requested demand of a studied large load by 2032 (Year 6)?	ERCOT will make every effort to prepare an actionable transmission plan that reliably serves all studied Large Loads requesting energization through 2032.  If ERCOT cannot identify a timely transmission solution to serve a portion of a Large Load's request by 2032, then the unserved portion will not be allocated.  That unserved portion can be included in the next interconnection study.  
		29	Why does the Load Commissioning Plan in the Batch Zero Load Information Form start in 2028?  What if the Large Load is energizing and ramping before 2028?	The Load Commissioning Plan in the Batch Zero Load Information Form captures the information that ERCOT requires to conduct the Batch Zero Interconnection Study, which will study years 2028-2032.  If the ILLE is energizing and ramping in 2026 or 2027, it should ensure that the Interconnecting TSP and ERCOT have the most up-to-date schedule.
		30	What is the correct MW amount to enter for each year for the TPIT-adjusted LLIS Load Commissioning Plan?	On the LCP New tab of the Batch Zero Load Information Form (LIF), an ILLE that relies on a LLIS to qualify as either base load or studied load needs to complete the table titled "LLIS Load Commissioning Plan (LCP) as modified by TPIT."  For each of the five rows representing years 2028-2032, the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP should enter the highest peak demand during the year reflected in its LLIS LCP even if this MW demand level is contingent on a transmission upgrade scheduled to come into service after the summer peak.
		31	When will ERCOT stop reviewing and approving interconnection studies in accordance with the Large Load Interconnection Study process under PGRR115?	ERCOT will halt all reviews of LLIS studies at 11:59 p.m. on July 10, 2026.  No approvals will be issued after that time.
		32	May an ILLE with a Large Load included in a completed and endorsed RPG study request additional demand beyond the demand above what was included and evaluated as part of the RPG?	No. An ILLE included in a completed and endorsed RPG study cannot rely on that RPG approval to request additional demand above the MW demand included in the RPG review.  To request additional demand, the ILLE would need an additional study to evaluate that request.
		33	Does the value of the LCP need to reflect the highest load value for the year or the highest load value up through the summer peak?	For any LCP that is submitted on behalf of a Batch Zero ILLE - whether it is base or studied load - enter the maximum amount of load that is expected to be consumed that calendar year (i.e., peak demand that is expected to be reached).
		34	In the Batch Zero LIF, Section 3 - Eligibility Requirements, Row 23 (Preliminary Load Commissioning Plan (LCP)): how should the TSP submit the initial schedule for a Large Load seeking base load inclusion?	An initial LCP is required for base load inclusion under the eligibility paths in Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)–(g). What the TSP submits depends on the entry path:
LLIS entry: The TSP should submit an initial LCP consistent with the LLIS study.
RPG entry: The TSP should submit the ILLE's latest demand request for the years preceding the in-service date of the final RPG upgrade.
		35	If an ILLE has a power factor better than the one used in its studies, does that negatively impact its Batch Zero status?	An improved power factor will not negatively impact a Large Loads study status or any study approvals.  A power factor improvement will not allow earlier energization or increased demand.  Those results will remain as previously studied.  For this evaluation, ERCOT considers a power factor closer to unity an improved power factor.
		36	What does an Interconnecting TSP need to do if it has a Large Load that it believes has a qualifying study under Section 9.2.1.4(3)(d)?	If an Interconnecting TSP believes that a Large Load has a qualifying study under Section 9.2.1.4(3)(d), the Interconnecting TSP must complete the dedicated attestation form available on the Large Load Integration webpage.  The form must be notarized and the Interconnecting TSP's submission must be accompanied by the supporting documentation that supports the attestation.  ERCOT will review the attestation and supporting documents to whether the Large Load is eligible for inclusion in Batch Zero under Section 9.2.1.4(3)(d).  The Large Load must have satisfied the requirements in Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e) or (f) and submitted dynamic model data by July 10.  The Interconnecting TSP should mark "completed" in Section 3, Row 5 of the Batch Zero LIF.
	Commitment and notice requirements post-Batch Zero Interconnection Study	37	What is required to satisfy the commitment requirements under the Batch Zero Process? 	Following completion of the Batch Zero Interconnection Study, an ILLE with studied load must execute an interconnection agreement meeting the requirements of P.U.C. SUBST. R. 25.194 and accept the allocated peak Demand and schedule reflected in the updated Load Commissioning Plan (LCP). The applicable Interconnecting DSP or TSP must then provide ERCOT a notarized attestation confirming the required commitments were satisfied by the applicable deadline. Additional requirements apply for projects electing PCLR or WLPUN treatment. Large Loads that fail to satisfy the applicable commitment requirements are excluded from the Batch Zero Refinement Study and are not eligible for Initial Energization unless included in a future batch process.
		38	Does the “notice to proceed with the construction of all required interconnection Facilities” (9.2.1.1(1)(e)(iv)) need to be immediately effective?	Yes.  A binding notice to proceed must be issued by July 10, 2026.  The notice must be an unconditional authorization to proceed.  The notice may not be contingent on any unsatisfied condition precedent that could prevent or void the need for construction.  However, construction of the facilities may commence on a future date.  
		39	If the Interconnecting TSP is not able to provide direct interconnection costs and a facility schedule setting forth the specific facilities applicable to those costs by July 10, 2026, but if the interconnection agreement (or equivalent agreement) confirms that these issues will be addressed in the future and the ILLE agrees to issue a Notice to Proceed (NTP) by July 10, will the NTP satisfy the PGRR 145 requirements?	No.  The direct interconnection facilities and their associated costs must be identified before the ILLE can give a meaningful NTP.  An agreement to resolve these matters later, even with the developer's consent, does not satisfy this requirement because the developer cannot meaningfully commit to proceed without knowing what it is committing to.
	Dynamic model and technical submission requirements	40	What dynamic model information is required for Batch Zero participation? 	By July 10, 2026, the ILLE must provide ERCOT and the Interconnecting TSP dynamic data, including the necessary models, parameters, and supporting technical documentation required for accurate representation of the Large Load. The data must be compatible with the version of the planning and operations model software specified in the Dynamics Working Group Procedure Manual in effect on March 4, 2026. If a prior dynamic stability study exists, the Interconnecting TSP must also provide ERCOT by July 24, 2026 a written determination regarding whether the submitted dynamic data is expected to adversely impact the prior study results. ERCOT has prepared a form Interconnecting TSPs must use to inform ERCOT whether a prior stability study was conducted, and if it was, whether the updated dynamic data adversely impacts the study results. ERCOT may notify the ILLE of any deficiencies by August 7, 2026, with a cure period extending through August 31, 2026.
		41	Will ERCOT provide confirmation when model submissions are received? 	PGRR145 does not expressly require ERCOT to provide formal receipt confirmations for dynamic model submissions. ERCOT is currently developing the submission and communication process for Batch Zero implementation, including package tracking and confirmation procedures. Stakeholders should expect additional guidance as implementation activities progress.
		42	What happens if a Large Load changes its load technology, configuration, or operating characteristics after studies have been completed?
	ERCOT may evaluate whether the change adversely impacts prior study assumptions, dynamic model performance, or eligibility determinations. Material changes may require additional review and could affect study validity or Batch Zero classification.
		43	For co-located load and generation projects, what should be included in the dynamic model submission? 	For co-located projects, the submitted dynamic model should include sufficient information to accurately represent both the Large Load and the associated generation configuration, including all relevant operating characteristics necessary for ERCOT to evaluate stability and system impacts. Additional generation-related modeling requirements may also apply under Section 6.9 and the applicable FIS requirements.

		44	Who is responsible for submitting dynamic models to ERCOT — the ILLE or the TSP? 	Under Section 9.2.2(3), the ILLE is responsible for providing the dynamic data, models, parameters, and supporting technical documentation to both ERCOT and the Interconnecting TSP by July 10, 2026. If a prior dynamic stability study exists, the Interconnecting TSP must also provide ERCOT by July 24, 2026 a written determination regarding whether the submitted dynamic data is expected to adversely impact the prior study results. ERCOT has prepared a form Interconnecting TSPs must use to inform ERCOT whether a prior stability study was conducted, and if it was, whether the updated dynamic data adversely impacts the study results.

		45	What happens if required dynamic model information is incomplete by the July 10 deadline? 	Under Section 9.2.2(3)(a), if ERCOT determines that submitted dynamic data is deficient, ERCOT must notify the ILLE no later than August 7, 2026. The ILLE then has until August 31, 2026 to cure the deficiency. Failure to resolve the deficiency by August 31, 2026 results in removal of the associated Large Load from the Batch Zero Interconnection Study.

		46	Will a Large Computational Load's (LCL) allocation be impacted if the LCL is unable to update its model to show compliance with NOGRR282 prior to the end of Batch Zero?	NOGRR282 compliance is separate and distinct from Batch Zero timelines and eligibility.  If NOGRR282 is approved by the PUCT, a LCL will be required to comply with the voltage and frequency ride-through requirements of NOGRR282 unless the LCL is entitled to an exemption as provided in the NOGRR.  A LCL subject to study and allocation under Section 9.2.1.2 in Batch Zero that is not exempt from the ride-through requirements will need to submit models that demonstrate compliance with those requirements to qualify for a QSA after Batch Zero.  A LCL that is included in Batch Zero as base load should review NOGRR282 and the QSA timelines to determine whether it is subject to NOGRR282 compliance.  ERCOT is highlighting the NOGRR282 performance requirements to inform LCLs about the relevant timing; however, this does not affect the allocation process for Batch Zero.

		47	For an existing Large Load that has energized, if it did not have a dynamic model previously, does it need to have one prepared to submit by July 10?	Whether or not the Large Load previously submitted a dynamic model, a Large Load that is already energized does not need to submit a dynamic model for Batch Zero.  Of course, ERCOT encourages a model submission that accurately reflects the characteristics of the Large Load.
		48	Must an SSO study be complete and validated for a Large Load to be included in Batch Zero as Base Load?	No.  If an SSO assessment is required for the Large Load, the study, any required mitigation plan, and associated countermeasures must be completed prior to initial energization. PGRR145 explicitly lists completion of required SSO studies and mitigation as a prerequisite for Initial Energization.
		49	If the Large Load composition or type changes, e.g., from a crypto to AI load, is the only requirement to submit a new dynamic model to the QSA and obtain ERCOT's approval that the Large Load change is acceptable prior to making the change?	At this time, the applicable requirements are those in Section 9.6(2), "During Continuing Operations," and Section 9.2.3, "Modification of Large Load Information," of PGRR145. Please follow those processes for the proposed change.  Additionally, if the proposed change falls within the categories described in Section 9.2.1, "Applicability of the Large Load Interconnection Study Process," please follow the applicable process outlined in that section. It is unclear when the proposed change would occur. Please note that PGRR144 is currently under stakeholder review and is not yet effective. If PGRR144 becomes effective, ERCOT expects applicable entities to follow the requirements and processes established by PGRR144.
		50	How do planned network upgrades for the corresponding Large Load's request impact the generator's eligibility to interconnect? PGRR 120 prohibits interconnection of new generation to series compensated lines.  If the interconnection of a Large Load will require network upgrades for the load request, how does this affect the generator's eligibility to interconnect?	Whether the proposed generator satisfies the requirements of Planning Guide Section 5.2.10 depends on the transmission topology that will exist when the generator is interconnected. 
For questions regarding generator interconnection eligibility and the applicable interconnection process, please coordinate with the ERCOT Resource Integration team and the interconnecting TSP.

		51	What supporting technical documents and information are needed in the dynamic model package?	Supporting technical documents and information includes documents that help understand, check, and accurately represent the submitted dynamic model and the associated facility or equipment. This documentation should include, but is not limited to:
•	User-Defined Model (UDM) documentation, such as user manuals, model descriptions, control logic, block diagrams, or software documentation that explains the model implementation and operation.
•	Technology-specific documentation, if available, provided by the equipment manufacturer or developer, describing the control systems or operating characteristics of the equipment or technologies such as ride-through solution.
•	⁠PSS/E load flow (.raw) file compatible with version 35, and/or an IDEV or Python file containing the project configuration and transformer model data required by the ERCOT Dynamic Working Group Large Load Data Survey.
		52	What if dynamic data and files are too large to email or blocked by email server?	If files (such as .dll files) cannot be submitted by email due to file type restrictions or file size limitations, please note this in your submission. ERCOT LLI Team will coordinate with the ILLE to arrange a secure shared drive for uploading those files. 
Please note that ERCOT does not maintain a dedicated shared drive for all submissions. Shared drives will be created only when needed to facilitate the transfer of files that cannot be submitted via email. This approach helps ensure secure file management and avoids the accumulation of unrelated or unnecessary files.
		53	Which PSS/e version should the dynamic model support?	For Batch Zero, all submitted models must be compatible with PSS/E Version 35.
		54	Row 22 in Section 3 of the Batch Zero Load Information Form requires the “Full technical data package.”  What does the “Full technical data package” include?	Row 22 has no purpose now.  The requirement is duplicative of data already captured elsewhere on the form.  However, the ILLE should consult with the interconnecting TSP or DSP to determine whether additional technical information is required.
		55	What is the deadline for ILLE submission of dynamic data to ERCOT?	The dynamic data must be submitted to ERCOT on or before Friday, July 10, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CDT.  According to Planning Guide Section 9.2.2(3), the ILLE must provide dynamic data to ERCOT by July 10, 2026.  So long as the email to submit models or email to request a link is received to BatchZero@ercot.com by deadline (July 10, 2359), then the link will be provided by Monday July 13 to complete submission by close of business on July 13.  Please include the Large Load's BZ number in the request.
		56	May an ILLE provide ERCOT with a link to a secure share website to provide its Batch Zero dynamic data submissions to ERCOT?	No.  If an ILLE’s dynamic data submission to the batchzero@ercot.com mailbox is not initially successful, the ILLE should submit another email to batchzero@ERCOT.com without any attachments that requests a secure share drive link.  So long as the email to submit models or email to request a link is received to BatchZero@ercot.com by deadline (July 10, 2359), then link will be provided by Monday July 13 to complete submission by close of business July 13.  Please include the Large Load's BZ number in the request.
		57	May an Interconnecting TSP submit its steady state data in file formats other than IDEVs?	Yes, ERCOT will accept steady-state data in .py formats.
		58	Is an Interconnecting TSP required to submit an IDEV for Tier 1, 2, or 3 RPG projects?	No.  If an RPG project is approved, ERCOT already has the IDEV.  For RPG projects that have not been approved or endorsed, ERCOT will coordinate with the relevant Interconnecting TSP to determine if the RPG project will help resolve transmission needs identified in the Batch Zero study.  ERCOT may consider those project alternatives when determining how to address reliability issues in the Batch Zero study.
		59	Is an Interconnecting TSP required to submit IDEVs for Tier 4 projects?	Yes, the Interconnecting TSP should submit IDEVs for Tier 4 transmission improvements that are associated with the LCP for a Batch Zero base load.
		60	How should an Interconnecting TSP model a co-located Large Load that is not pursuing WLPUN status?	The Interconnecting TSP does not need to include the generation in its IDEV submission.  ERCOT will include the generation in accordance with Planning Guide Section 6.9 and Planning Guide Revision Request 127, Addition of Proposed Generation to the Planning Models.
		61	May the Interconnecting TSP work with an ILLE to address a dynamic model that the TSP would determine to have an adverse impact on an earlier stability study?	No.  If an ILLE submitted an updated dynamic model on July 10 the TSP should evaluate whether the updated model has an adverse impact on the prior stability study and report its impact determination on July 24. 
		62	For which Large Load types is the Interconnecting TSP required to submit the attestation whether the dynamic model adversely impacts the previous stability study?	The Interconnecting TSP is required to submit the stability study assessment required in Section 9.2.2(3) if (1) a dynamic stability study on the Large Load has previously been performed and (2) the Large Load is potentially included in Batch Zero under Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(d)-(1)(g) plus studied loads under Section 9.2.1.2.  The Interconnecting TSP must use the ERCOT-Interconnecting TSP Dynamic Stability Study Form and select "Complete" on Section 3, Row 26 of the Batch Zero LIF.    
	 Communications and process management	63	What email address or communication channel should stakeholders use for Batch Zero questions and submissions? 	Interconnecting TSPs or DSPs and ILLEs should send Batch Zero-related questions and submissions to the following email addresses:
-LLWG_Feedback@ercot.com for general Batch Zero implementation questions, stakeholder feedback, and process clarification requests (Interconnecting TSPs and DSPs should not use this email address for eligibility submission packages);
- LargeLoadInterconnection@ercot.com for existing LLIS process questions, including ongoing study reviews, dynamic model submissions, and interconnection study coordination (will cease operation after July 10); and
- BatchZero@ercot.com for formal Batch Zero eligibility submissions by the designated Interconnecting DSP or TSP, as applicable.
		64	How will ERCOT and TSPs standardize subjective validation criteria across Large Loads?	ERCOT, in consultation with Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs, is continuing to develop implementation guidance regarding validation standards and supporting documentation requirements. ERCOT may request supporting materials or perform additional verification.  ERCOT has prepared attestation and Load Information Forms to standardize the intake of information.
		65	Should the Interconnecting TSP copy the ILLE on Batch Zero submission communications with ERCOT?	Copying the ILLE on submission-related communications would be considered good practice. Additional guidance regarding communication expectations between ERCOT, Interconnecting DSPs/TSPs, and ILLEs may be provided during implementation.  However, ILLEs should not send attestations or other information directly to ERCOT.  Information should be sent through the Interconnecting DSP and TSP, as applicable.

		66	Will ERCOT provide provisional feedback before PUCT approval of PGRR145?	ERCOT may review submitted materials and provide preliminary feedback regarding completeness, deficiencies, or additional information needs. However, final Batch Zero eligibility determinations and classification decisions are contingent upon the PUCT's approval of the revision requests and completion of ERCOT's validation process.

		67	Will ERCOT consider an ILLE's submission of the eligibility package directly to ERCOT?	Except for the dynamic model information, ERCOT will only review the completed eligibility package sent by the Interconnecting TSP or DSP.  The ILLE should not copy ERCOT on its submission to the Interconnecting TSP or DSP.
		68	Where can I find ERCOT's forms required for Batch Zero?	The forms prepared by ERCOT can be found on the Large Load Integration page: https://www.ercot.com/services/rq/large-load-integration 
		69	How does an ILLE confirm that its eligibility package is submitted to ERCOT by July 24?	The ILLE and Interconnecting TSP and DSP should coordinate in advance of the July 10th and July 24th deadlines to ensure that the Interconnecting TSP and DSP are prepared to submit all required information to ERCOT on or before July 24th.
		70	The Batch Zero Load Information Form and Attestation Forms require the “ILLE Name.”  What is the ILLE name?	The “ILLE Name” refers to the legal business name of the entity seeking interconnection of a Large Load.  This is different from the Large Load facility name, which may be the name the ILLE assigns to the development/future facility. 
		71	If the Large Load does not have a formal address yet, can it use an address associated with co-located generation or are coordinates better?	Street address is acceptable.  The main intention is the correct identification of the substation.
		72	What happens if my TSP/DSP does not submit my materials on July 24?	Per Section 9.2.1.3, ERCOT shall not include any Large Load that meets the requirements described in Section 9.2.1.1 or 9.2.1.2 if the Interconnecting TSP or Interconnecting DSP fails to provide to ERCOT all information required by Section 9.2.2 on or before July 24, 2026.  The ILLE should consult with its Interconnecting TSP or Interconnecting DSP to ensure they have accurate and complete information to submit to ERCOT on or before July 24, 2026.
		73	Who may submit LIFs, IDEVs, or attestations to ERCOT?	ERCOT will accept LIFs, IDEVs, or attestations only when they are (1) submitted by an Interconnecting DSP or TSP, and (2) received in the batchzero@ercot.com mailbox.
		74	How will ERCOT handle receipt of LIFs, IDEVs, or attestations from someone other than the Interconnecting DSP or TSP?	ERCOT will not use them in any way. The Planning Guide requires that the Interconnecting DSP or TSP submit the information. A submission from any other source does not satisfy that requirement.
		75	How will ERCOT handle receipt of LIFs, IDEVs, or attestations submitted to a mailbox other than  batchzero@ercot.com?	ERCOT will not use them in any way. ERCOT has designated batchzero@ercot.com as the exclusive mailbox for Batch Zero submissions and processes only what arrives there. Anything sent elsewhere will not be considered.
		76	In the Batch Zero Load Information Form (LIF), Section 3 - Eligibility Requirements, Row 36 (IDEV files): if the TSP intends to submit the IDEV files separately and later than the LIF file, how should it complete the 'Completion Status' and 'Supporting File Name(s)' columns?	The Interconnecting TSP should select 'Complete' in the Column J pull-down menu.  The Interconnecting TSP does not need to enter anything in Column K.  Column K can remain blank.  However, the Interconnecting TSP must submit the IDEV with the Large Load included on or before July 24.
		77	If an Interconnecting TSP needs to request a BZ number for a Large Load, how should that be requested?	The Interconnecting TSP should submit a request for a BZ number to ERCOT via the BatchZero@ercot.com email box.  The request should include identifying information about the Large Load, including the ILLE name, requested MW, eligibility path, and a qualifying study.
		78	The Stability Validity Form includes a signature block.  Is an officer required to sign the form?	No, per the signature block, a representative, official, officer, or other authorized person with binding authority may sign.  The form does not require an officer to sign.
		79	Section 3, Row 4 of the Batch Zero LIF requires the Interconnecting TSP to indicate whether the Large Load has a "Complete and Valid Study Determination."  What does ERCOT expect the Interconnecting TSP to provide here?	The Interconnecting TSP should use this row to confirm that it believes the Large Load has a complete and valid set of interconnection studies as required by Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(i) and (1)(f)(i).
		80	Section 3, Row 5 of the Batch Zero LIF appears as optional.  When is it required?	If the Interconnecting TSP is submitting a Large Load as qualifying under Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(e) or (1)(f) and the qualifying study is under Section 9.2.1.4(3)(d), then the Interconnecting TSP should so indicate through this field. 
		81	How should the Interconnecting TSP complete Section 3, Row 33 of the Batch Zero LIF for a Large Load eligible under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(b)?	The Interconnecting TSP may select "Not Applicable" in Column J.
		82	Does ERCOT expect the Interconnecting TSP to test the veracity of any of the ILLE attestations?	No.  However, using the Batch Zero LIF, the Interconnecting TSP must confirm the ILLE has: (1) attested to meeting the requirements for the selected eligibility path, (2) posted any required financial security, and (3) satisfied any financial obligations for direct interconnection costs.  In addition, a reminder that 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.503(d) requires market participants to provide accurate and truthful communications and dealings with ERCOT.
		83	Does a Large Load qualifying under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(c) eligibility path need to complete Row 34?
	No.  A Large Load qualifying under the Section 9.2.1.1(1)(c) eligibility path does not need to complete Row 34.  Selected "not applicable" in Column J and leave Column K blank.  
		84	Section 3, Row 5 of the Batch Zero LIF appears as optional.  When is it required?	If the Interconnecting TSP is submitting a Large Load as qualifying under Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(e) or (1)(f) and the qualifying study is under Section 9.2.1.4(3)(d), then the Interconnecting TSP should so indicate through this field. 
		85	How should the Interconnecting TSP complete Section 3, Row 33 of the Batch Zero LIF for a Large Load eligible under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(b)?	The Interconnecting TSP may select "Not Applicable" in Column J.
		86	Does ERCOT expect the Interconnecting TSP to test the veracity of any of the ILLE attestations?	No.  However, using the Batch Zero LIF, the Interconnecting TSP must confirm the ILLE has: (1) attested to meeting the requirements for the selected eligibility path, (2) posted any required financial security, and (3) satisfied any financial obligations for direct interconnection costs.  In addition, a reminder that 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.503(d) requires market participants to provide accurate and truthful communications and dealings with ERCOT.
		87	Does a Large Load qualifying under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(c) eligibility path need to complete Row 34?
	No.  A Large Load qualifying under the Section 9.2.1.1(1)(c) eligibility path does not need to complete Row 34.  Selected "not applicable" in Column J and leave Column K blank.  
	Financial security and cost responsibility	88	Is Batch Zero financial security refundable?	PGRR145 does not address refundability of financial security.  For information about the timing and amount of refundable security, stakeholders should refer to proceedings at the Public Utility Commission of Texas, including Project Nos. 58481, Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards Under PURA § 37.0561, and 59142, Review of ERCOT's Interconnection Processes for Large Loads.

		89	Who is responsible for facility studies, contribution in aid of construction (CIAC) calculations, and related upgrade cost estimates?	Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs are responsible for conducting any required facility studies, estimating direct interconnection costs and applicable CIAC obligations, and providing an estimate of upgrade costs. ERCOT will not perform facility studies as part of the Batch Zero Interconnection Study. ILLEs should coordinate directly with their Interconnecting DSP or TSP regarding facility study scope, timing, cost estimates, and financial obligations.

		90	Is the financial security required under 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi) and the financial responsibility under 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vii) separate and distinct?	Yes, they are distinct financial commitment requirements.  
		91	If an ILLE modifies its LCP to show a lower MW amount before July 10, can it also lower its posted security or receive a refund for a portion of its direct interconnection costs?	PGRR145 does not address the release of financial security or refundability of direct interconnection costs. The ILLE's recourse is with its Interconnecting TSP or DSP directly.
		92	Will the financial security for base load change as a result of the Batch Zero Interconnection Study?	ERCOT does not intend to estimate new financial security requirements for Large Loads entering Batch Zero as base load.  However, the PUCT's rulemakings could establish different requirements.
		93	Do Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vii) and 9.2.1.1(1)(f)(v) prohibit CIAC from being offset by standard contribution or other allowance only if the ILLE does not have an executed interconnection agreement or equivalent agreement before July 10, 2026?	Yes, those two provisions prohibit CIAC from being offset by a standard contribution or other allowance unless the Interconnecting DSP or TSP and ILLE have executed an interconnection agreement or equivalent agreement on or before July 10, 2026.
		94	For a base load that must post financial security, is the $50,000/MW sufficient to satisfy the requirements for both (a) financial security for system upgrades (required under Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(e)(vi)) and (b) direct interconnection costs (required under Planning Guide Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vii))?	No.  The requirements in Sections 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi) and (vii) are distinct and the financial obligations must be addressed separately.  In the case of the financial security required under Section 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi), the ILLE must post financial security equal to $50,000/MW if the TSP is unable to estimate the cost of the necessary system upgrades.  The same answer applies to Section 9.2.1.1(1)(f)(iv) and (v).
		95	What is the last possible date for the ILLE to post financial security for studied load?	Section 9.2.1.2(1)(c) requires the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP to inform ERCOT that the ILLE posted the required financial security for system upgrades on or before July 24, 2026. This is the same deadline for the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP to submit all required data to ERCOT.  An ILLE who waits until July 24, 2026, to post financial security risks exclusion from Batch Zero.  Thus, the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP may establish an earlier deadline.
		96	Is it acceptable for an Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP to accept a corporate or parental guarantee where the guarantor has a rating from Standard and Poor’s, Fitch, or Moody’s if the credit rating is for a different country?	An ILLE may only rely on a corporate or parental guaranty where the guarantor has a U.S.- or international-based credit rating from one of the three main credit rating agencies, Standard & Poor’s, Fitch, or Moody’s.  Absent that, the ILLE may look at the other options listed in PGRR145 that are acceptable to the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnection TSP.
		97	Several places in Planning Guide Sections 9.2.1.1, 9.2.1.2, and 9.3.1 address the posting of financial security.  How will ERCOT determine whether the financial security posting was complete by the applicable deadline?	ERCOT will consider the posting of required financial security complete when the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP possesses the funding in its accounts or has irrevocable access to the funds under the terms of the posting.  If the Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP cannot use or draw on the funds or any transfer is recallable, the posting is not complete.
		98	What is the correct way to complete Section 3, Row 15, Transmission upgrade financial security?  Are any documents required?	The Interconnecting TSP should select “complete” in the Column J pull-down menu.  The Interconnecting TSP may, but is not required, to provide supporting documentation with its submissions to ERCOT on July 24.  However, under Planning Guide Section 9.1(8), ERCOT will conduct a verification process and may later request supporting documentation to determine the veracity of ILLE and TSP claims.  In addition, a reminder that 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.503(d) requires market participants to provide accurate and truthful communications and dealings with ERCOT.
	TPIT	99	Are TSPs required to add in TPIT transmission projects included in the LCP for Batch Zero base load, studied load, or both?	TSPs must include or update transmission projects for qualifying Batch Zero base loads, not studied loads. For energized large loads, if an energized Large Load requires upgrades to energize additional increments, then the necessary transmission projects to serve the Large Load should be in TPIT to support the LCP. ERCOT recognizes that a TSPs may not know which loads will ultimately be base load vs. studied load. If in doubt, the TSPs should add the transmission projects to TPIT.
		100	How will a TSP know to update in TPIT a transmission project included in the LCP of a Large Load not located in its territory?	TSPs should coordinate with their neighbors to ensure transmission projects necessary to support their customer’s LCPs are updated in TPIT.  ERCOT cannot provide a unified list of transmission projects included in every Large Load’s LCP. 
		101	If a transmission project included in a Large Load’s LCP is not submitted by July 2, 2026, PGRR145 Section 9.2.1.1(2)(c)(ii)(B) states that ERCOT may request the TSP provide an estimated ISD in lieu of assuming a 2034 date. Is this still applicable?	#VALUE!
		102	How will ERCOT model Tier 1, 2, and 3 RPG projects that have not completed RPG review?	ERCOT will not model Tier 1, 2, and 3 RPG projects that have not completed RPG review in the Batch Zero initial cases. However, TSPs may include such projects in TPIT if they are included in a Large Load’s LCP.  ERCOT may consider those project alternatives when determining how to address reliability issues in the Batch Zero study.
		103	Is it acceptable for these transmission projects to be submitted as “Conceptual” in MOD?  	Yes.  TSPs should flag these transmission projects as conceptual in MOD with the "Transmission Status" field.
		104	For the TPIT submission, is just the baseline transmission project data needed or is the actual topology needed as well?	Initially, TSPs need to submit or update the metadata for the transmission projects.  The technical details of the transmission project may be updated later.
		105	Should the LLI ID or Batch Zero number be in TPIT/the MOD project information?	In order to protect confidential customer, Batch Zero Numbers should not be included in the TPIT/MOD project information.
		106	Should these transmission projects be included in the October SSWG cases?	ERCOT will follow up on this.
		107	If a station must be constructed to serve a Large Load, should both the station and upgrades needed to serve the Large Load be included in TPIT or should just the upgrades (no station) be included?  An example would be a cut in station.	Only the upgrade needed to serve the Large Load should be included in TPIT. The POI station will be assumed to be included based on the in-service date of the load.
		108	If an RPG project to support the interconnection of a Large Load has been submitted but the transmission upgrades to serve the ILLEs' LCPs for these loads are more of a placeholder/interim type, what should the TSP provide in TPIT?	The TSP should include the transmission projects with the best-known information.  
		109	Is there a plan for the ad-hoc TPIT report to be updated for Large Loads that become base loads between July 2 and July 10? Similarly, is there a plan for Large Loads that are considered base load on July 2 that may be changed to allocated when other loads reach Section 9.5 by July 10?
